In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of $\mathcal{M}$-theory and IIA string backgrounds that preserve four supersymmetries.
the study of the geometry of $\mathcal{M}$-theory and type IIA string compactifications with non-vanishing fluxes, and with the construction of solutions to the corresponding field equations.
the construction of supersymmetric backgrounds of M theory, type IIA strings, and heterotic strings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all known $\mathcal{ N}=1$ backgrounds with internal fluxes can be derived from the formalism developed in the present paper.
all the $\mathcal{ N}=1$ backgrounds found so far are special cases of our general construction.
all the known solutions of M theory and IIA supergravity with fluxes and with a 4-dimensional Minkowski background are included in our classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

all $\mathcal{ N}=1$ backgrounds with irreducible internal mani-folds and fluxes can be obtained by starting with a Ricci-flat manifold, turning on the fluxes, and then solving the flow equations for the metric and the dilaton.
we have a systematic method to construct $\mathcal{ N }=1$ backgrounds with fluxes.
we have provided a general framework for constructing $\mathcal{M}$-flux backgrounds of type IIA strings and M theory, and have shown that the Hitchin flow is a special case of our general formalism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of flux does not necessarily imply that one has to consider non-Kahler manifolds.
the existence of a nontrivial flux requires the internal space to possess nontrivial torsion, which is in general not a closed form.

the internal manifolds of $\mathcal{M}$-theory and type IIA supergravity with fluxes are always of product structure, and hence, they can always be viewed as a warped product of a four-dimensional Minkowskian space-time and a curved internal manifold.
